::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Read what the Sennheiser MD 421 is.
2. Learn how it hears: pattern, proximity, off axis.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.
4. Look up famous uses.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- The **MD 421**: a dynamic **cardioid**, **30-17,000 Hz ±3 dB** (Wikipedia, "Sennheiser MD 421").
- A five-position **bass roll-off** ring from **M** (music) to **S** (speech) (Wikipedia).
- Used at the 1966 Eurovision (Udo Jürgens) and in numbers on The Concert for Bangladesh (Wikipedia).

## How it hears

- Wikipedia: almost linear in the bass up to 1 kHz, then a smooth upper-mid rise.
- The bass switch steps take away low end (step amounts here are the site's).
- Close up, a directional mic gains **bass**: the **proximity effect** (Wikipedia, "Proximity effect (audio)"). Slide the distance and watch the low end of the graph rise.
- The response graph is the maker's published chart **digitised approximately** (the charts are pictures; the points here follow their shape as remembered: unverified).

## The mic

The Sennheiser MD 421 drawn after photos (proportions approximate, no logos), with its switches: click them. Drag the blue mic in the room (or use the Distance slider; the wheel or Angle turns it), choose a source and a room, press **▶ Hear it**. Voice is generated (the band has no singer); snare and kick are the band's kit; the guitar is the site's amp model. Nobody has compared the sound with a real mic.

```{=html}
<div class="mic" data-mic="md421" data-src="snare"></div>
```

## Guided tour

```{=html}
<div class="mic-step" data-mic="md421" data-set="{&quot;bass&quot;:&quot;M&quot;}" data-place="{&quot;dist&quot;:0.05,&quot;angle&quot;:30}" data-src="snare"><p><b>M, 5 cm, 30° (a tom).</b> Full.</p></div>
<div class="mic-step" data-mic="md421" data-set="{&quot;bass&quot;:&quot;S&quot;}" data-place="{&quot;dist&quot;:0.05,&quot;angle&quot;:30}" data-src="snare"><p><b>S.</b> Most of the bass off.</p></div>
<div class="mic-step" data-mic="md421" data-set="{&quot;bass&quot;:&quot;3&quot;}" data-place="{&quot;dist&quot;:0.03,&quot;angle&quot;:0}" data-src="guitar"><p><b>On the amp, step 3.</b></p></div>
<div class="mic-step" data-mic="md421" data-set="{&quot;bass&quot;:&quot;M&quot;}" data-place="{&quot;dist&quot;:0.05,&quot;angle&quot;:0}" data-src="kick"><p><b>On the kick.</b></p></div>
```

## Works Cited

<!-- works-cited: written by scripts/works-cited.py -->
::: {.works-cited}
"Microphone." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microphone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microphone). Polar patterns as first-order sums: the cardioid = omni + figure-8, the figure-8's negative rear signal cancelling; ribbons' symmetric front and rear pickup.

"Sennheiser MD 421." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sennheiser_MD_421](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sennheiser_MD_421). Cardioid dynamic, 30-17,000 Hz ±3 dB; five-step bass roll-off M to S; Merci, Chérie (1966 Eurovision); The Concert for Bangladesh.

**For students**

"Proximity effect (audio)." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proximity_effect_(audio)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proximity_effect_(audio)). Bass rises close to a directional mic; caused by the ports; not a true omni, but not necessarily absent on a multipattern mic's summed omni.
:::
<!-- /works-cited -->
